reasoning: No pictures, audio, or frame anchors are supplied, so this is a pure text-to-video build with no image responsibilities and no replacement targets. The request asks only for a lighthouse keeper climbing the tower stairs in a storm and lighting the lamp; it does not request spoken or sung words, visible lettering, or score, so those scope slots remain false and no creative additions of speech or text are made. Balanced creativity permits shaping and ambience, so the fifteen seconds are broken into four shots that carry the climb and the lighting in a clear progression: the storm-bound tower, the ascent, the lamp catching, and the beam sweeping out. Camera modifiers are all explicit within the closed vocabulary.

shots.action: Rain lashes a tall stone lighthouse standing on a black rocky headland; huge waves burst white against the base and a fork of lightning flares behind the tower, briefly throwing the whole structure into silhouette before the dark closes back in.
subjects: the stone lighthouse on a rocky headland
the storm-driven sea and breaking waves
shots.what_changes: The shot opens on the storm-battered lighthouse and pushes gradually closer as lightning flares and the waves surge.

shots.action: Inside the tower, a soaked lighthouse keeper in a heavy coat and cap climbs the tight spiral staircase, one hand on the cold iron rail and the other holding a swaying lantern; the flame gutters with each gust that rattles the shuttered windows, and his boots strike the worn stone steps in a steady, laboring rhythm as he works his way upward.
subjects: the lighthouse keeper in a heavy coat and cap
the swinging lantern in his hand
the spiral stone staircase and iron rail
sync_sound: the creak of the lantern handle
shots.what_changes: The keeper ascends the spiral staircase, the lantern swinging and the storm audible against the shutters.

shots.action: In the lamp room the keeper sets the lantern down, grips the brass clockwork mechanism with both hands and turns the crank until it catches; he lifts the glass chimney, shields the wick from the draft with his palm, and the flame takes with a soft roar, swelling bright and throwing his face into warm relief as the great Fresnel lens begins to turn.
subjects: the lighthouse keeper at the lamp mechanism
the brass clockwork and Fresnel lens
sync_sound: the clack and whirr of the clockwork crank
the hiss of the wick catching
glass and brass rattling in the wind
the muffled roar of the storm outside
shots.what_changes: The lamp ignites and brightens, the lens begins rotating, and the keeper's face is lit warm against the cold blue storm light.

shots.action: The camera draws back through the lamp-room glass to the outside of the tower as the beam sweeps out in a long white arc across the heaving sea, cutting through the rain; the keeper stands small and silhouetted behind the turning lens, one hand still on the mechanism.
subjects: the silhouetted keeper in the lamp room
sync_sound: the low moan of wind around the tower
a faint mechanical hum from the turning lens
shots.what_changes: The beam swings out across the sea and the view widens to reveal the illuminated lighthouse holding its light against the storm.
